sections.title: Stage 1 foundations
sections.description: First steps with computers, algorithms, data and networks from Stage 1.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
questions.options: a kind of computer screen | a game you play outside | a picture drawn on paper | a set of clear steps in the right order
questions.correctAnswer: a set of clear steps in the right order
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a precise set of instructions, step by step, in the right order — like the steps for getting dressed.

questions.question: Asha wants to turn her algorithm into a program in ScratchJr. What does she change each step into?
questions.options: a block of code | a password | a new character | a photograph
questions.explanation: In ScratchJr, every step of your algorithm becomes one block. Joined together, the blocks make a program the computer can follow.

questions.question: A pictogram key says one picture means 2 books. A row shows 3 pictures. How many books is that?
questions.explanation: The key tells you what one picture is worth. Three pictures, each worth 2 books, make 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 books.

questions.question: Why do we keep a backup of important data?
questions.options: it is a safe spare copy in case the first one is lost | it makes the computer run faster | it turns the data into pictures | it deletes old data we do not need
questions.correctAnswer: it is a safe spare copy in case the first one is lost
questions.explanation: A backup is a spare copy kept somewhere safe. If the first copy is lost or broken, the backup is still there.

questions.question: Which of these is hardware — a part of the computer you can touch?
questions.options: a song saved on the computer | the keyboard | a drawing program | a story app
questions.explanation: Hardware is the parts you can touch, like the keyboard, mouse and screen. Apps, programs and files are software — the instructions inside.

questions.question: Which device is an output device — it gets things OUT of the computer for us?
questions.options: a keyboard | a microphone | a speaker | a mouse
questions.explanation: A speaker lets sound come OUT of the computer so we can hear it. A mouse, keyboard and microphone put things IN.

questions.question: An algorithm for making tea says: 1) Pour the tea into the cup, 2) Boil the water, 3) Put the tea in the pot. What is the bug?
questions.options: the algorithm is too short | the steps are in the wrong order | a computer cannot hold a teapot | there are too many cups
questions.correctAnswer: the steps are in the wrong order
questions.explanation: You cannot pour the tea before the water is boiled and the tea is in the pot. Swapping the steps into the right order fixes the bug.

questions.question: What is a network?
questions.options: a game about fishing nets | a very strong metal cable | devices joined together so they can share and send messages | one computer working all alone
questions.correctAnswer: devices joined together so they can share and send messages
questions.explanation: A network is devices joined together. Joined devices can send messages to each other and share things like a printer or photos.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Devices That Talk to Each Other

questions.question: A laptop joins the network through the air, with no cable at all. What do we call this kind of connection?
questions.options: offline | wireless | printed | wired
questions.explanation: Wireless means joined through the air with no cable — so the laptop can move around. Wired means joined with a cable.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Devices That Talk to Each Other

questions.question: In ScratchJr, which block makes a program begin when you tap the green flag?
questions.options: Repeat | Turn Right | Start on Green Flag | Hop
questions.explanation: The Start on Green Flag block is the starting block. When you tap the green flag, every program that begins with it runs.

questions.question: Which of these is numerical data — numbers we count or measure?
questions.options: names of fruits | kinds of animals | the ages of the children in a class | favourite colours
questions.correctAnswer: the ages of the children in a class
questions.explanation: Ages are numbers we can count and compare, so they are numerical data. Colours, names and kinds are categorical data — groups.

questions.question: Football shirts show the numbers 7 and 9. Why must we NOT add these numbers together?
questions.options: shirts are not allowed in data | the numbers are too small to add | they are just name tags for players, not amounts | adding only works on computers
questions.correctAnswer: they are just name tags for players, not amounts
questions.explanation: Shirt numbers are categorical data — they name a player, like a label. Only numerical data, amounts we count or measure, can be added up.

questions.question: Nadia's algorithm says: Move forward, Move forward, Move forward, Move forward. Which block makes this shorter but keeps the result the same?
questions.options: Turn left | Stop program | Repeat | Marker up
questions.explanation: When the same step happens again and again, Repeat does it for you. Repeat 4 times Move forward is shorter, and the result is the same.

questions.question: A message from a stranger arrives with a file attached. What should you do?
questions.options: reply and ask the stranger nicely | do not open it and tell a grown-up | send it on to all your friends | open it quickly to see what is inside
questions.correctAnswer: do not open it and tell a grown-up
questions.explanation: A file from someone we do not know could be malware — a program that is bad for the computer. Leave it closed and tell a grown-up.

questions.question: Which of these is private information you should keep to yourself online?
questions.options: the name of a storybook | your favourite colour | your home address | a drawing of a cat
questions.explanation: Your home address is private — it tells strangers where you live. Keep private things private, and ask a grown-up before sharing.

questions.question: A number machine adds 3 to any number you put in. Yusuf puts in 5. What comes out?
questions.explanation: Work through the steps like a computer: the input is 5, the machine adds 3, so the output is 5 + 3 = 8.

questions.question: What is a robot?
questions.options: any toy that has wheels | a computer screen that talks | a machine that does a task without help from a person | a person wearing a shiny metal suit
questions.correctAnswer: a machine that does a task without help from a person
questions.explanation: A robot is a machine that does a task by itself. It follows its instructions exactly — and it is not alive.

questions.question: Which kind of computer is small and easy to carry everywhere?
questions.options: a desktop computer | a television | a washing machine | a smartphone
questions.explanation: A smartphone is a small computer that fits in a pocket. A desktop computer is big and stays on a desk.

questions.question: Omar joins some Move blocks to a character in ScratchJr and runs the program. What does the character do?
questions.options: it prints a page | it turns the tablet off | it moves across the screen | nothing at all
questions.explanation: Each Move block is one step of code. When the program runs, the character follows the blocks and moves across the screen.

questions.question: Hodan sorts buttons by colour and counts 4 red buttons. On her block graph, how many blocks does she colour for red?
questions.explanation: On a block graph, you colour one block for each thing. Four red buttons means four blocks.

questions.question: Maya changes the number on a Move block from 2 to 6. What happens when she runs the program?
questions.options: the tablet turns off | the character changes colour | the character disappears | the character moves further
questions.explanation: Changing a step changes the outcome. A bigger number on a Move block means more steps, so the character moves further.

questions.question: What is the internet?
questions.options: a small toy telephone | a book about computers | the biggest network in the whole world | one single computer
questions.correctAnswer: the biggest network in the whole world
questions.explanation: The internet is the biggest network of all — lots and lots of computers joined together all around the world.

questions.question: What do we call a mistake in a program?
questions.options: a bug | a block | a spark | a prize
questions.explanation: A mistake in a program is called a bug. Finding and fixing a bug is called debugging — and everyone makes bugs sometimes!

questions.question: Which of these has a computer hiding inside that controls it?
questions.options: a washing machine | a wooden spoon | a paper book | a stone
questions.explanation: Computers hide inside many machines. The washing machine's computer tells it when to spin and when to stop.

questions.question: Ali counts birds with tally marks — one mark for each bird. He has 5 marks. How many birds did he count?
questions.explanation: Each tally mark stands for one bird. Five marks means Ali counted 5 birds.

questions.question: Zahra finishes her tap game in ScratchJr. What does testing her program mean?
questions.options: drawing a brand-new picture | trying the program to see if it works | deleting all the blocks | turning the tablet off
questions.correctAnswer: trying the program to see if it works
questions.explanation: Testing means trying your program — for a tap game, tap the character — and checking it does what you wanted.

questions.question: There is no internet at Ayan's house today — she is offline. Which of these will NOT work?
questions.options: drawing on paper | reading a paper book | watching an online video | playing with building blocks
questions.explanation: An online video needs the internet to reach the tablet. Offline, it will not play — but paper, books and blocks work just fine.

questions.question: A character must reach a star 3 squares to the right. Which list of steps gets it there?
questions.options: left, left, left | right, left, right | right, right, right | up, down, up
questions.explanation: The star is 3 squares to the right, so the algorithm needs three right steps in a row. Any other steps take the character the wrong way.
